html:
The Mattaponi are a Native American people of the Mattaponi River in eastern Virginia. In 1607 they were one of the tribes of the paramount chiefdom of Powhatan, which ruled most of the coastal plain when the English landed at Jamestown.

They lived in towns along the river, farming maize and fishing, and spoke an Algonquian language. After the wars with the colony they kept land along the river, and their reservation in King William County, held since the 1600s, is one of only two in Virginia, the other being that of the Pamunkey. Under the 1677 Treaty of Middle Plantation the two tribes still bring the governor of Virginia a tribute of game or fish each November. The Upper Mattaponi, upstream, are a separate tribe. Their neighbours include the Chickahominy.
